heard: Drop a needle on line paper and it tells you pie. No circle, no ruler, just a floor lines and a needle, and one man who got it far too right. Draw lines three centimeters apart. Drop a needle 2 .5 centimeters long, again and again, and count how often it lands across a line. Buffon proved the chances five over three pie, about 53 and 100. Turn that around and your count tells you pie. In 1901, Lazarini did it 3 ,408 times and got pie right to six decimals. Suspiciously right. An honest run that size is usually off by 0 .05. That's 3 .1. The giveaway 3 ,408 is 16 times 213. And 213 drops with 113 crossings, gives 355 over 113, a famous fraction for pie. Looks like he stopped when it fit. Six honest digits would take about 100 trillion drops. Drop 100 needles about how many cross a line.
